messages:
maria: FWIW hit a weird ClassCastException when streaming NDJSON from the Kotlin client in our shaded jar. stacktrace below, anyone seen this combo of OkHttp + Jackson + Gson shading?

kevin: can you paste the stacktrace and the shade config?

maria: stacktrace: 
```
java.lang.ClassCastException: com.redwood.libs.relocated.com.google.gson.internal.bind.TypeAdapters$33 cannot be cast to com.redwood.libs.relocated.com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonSerializer
	at com.redwood.app.stream.JsonStreamHandler.handle(JsonStreamHandler.kt:42)
	at com.redwood.client.StreamingResponseParser.parse(StreamingResponseParser.kt:88)
	...
```

maria: short context: we shade both gson and jackson (relocate) to avoid conflicts in downstream apps. seems fine in unit tests, but in integration with OkHttp streaming the parser tries to load a Jackson serializer but ends up with a shaded Gson TypeAdapter class. happens only with streaming endpoints (ndjson).

samir: hmm sounds like ServiceLoader/reflection resolution issue. Are you using any runtime module/plugin discovery (Jackson Module, or Jackson's `ObjectMapper.findAndRegisterModules()`)? shading can break resource files under META-INF/services or `META-INF/jackson-modules` so ServiceLoader might pick the wrong impl name.

maria: we call `ObjectMapper.registerModule(KotlinModule())` and also do `findAndRegisterModules()` in some shared helper. I bet that `findAndRegisterModules()` is picking up a relocated service file that points to the wrong classname (or duplicate entries).

kevin: two quick things to check: 1) ensure the shade `ServicesResourceTransformer` is enabled so META-INF/services are merged; 2) confirm relocation prefix is consistent for both libs so there aren't two different relocated copies of the same resource.

leo: also, for the auth/redirect streaming quirk we ran into before: OkHttp will drop `Authorization` on cross-host redirects by default. If your stream does a 307 to a different host, token can be missing and a downstream auth handler may generate a weird error that maps to a different path. If you see missing headers in logs try `followRedirects(false)` + manual redirect interceptor. Example:
```
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .followRedirects(false)
  .addInterceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request()
    val res = chain.proceed(req)
    if (res.isRedirect) {
      val newUrl = res.header("Location") ?: return@addInterceptor res
      val newReq = req.newBuilder()
        .url(newUrl)
        .header("Authorization", req.header("Authorization") ?: "")
        .build()
      return@addInterceptor chain.proceed(newReq)
    }
    res
  }
  .build()
```

jen: for the shading + Jackson/Gson clash my usual fix is: do not relocate classnames for those libs unless absolutely necessary. Instead: 1) exclude transitive versions from consumer libs and enforce a single version at the top-level, or 2) if you must relocate, make sure you also merge `META-INF/services` and `META-INF/jackson-modules` with the ServicesResourceTransformer and append the files so `findAndRegisterModules()` sees the relocated names.

samir: another option: stop relying on `findAndRegisterModules()`. Explicitly register the modules you need (KotlinModule, JavaTimeModule, etc.) by classname in your code after shading — since those are classes you control, you can call `objectMapper.registerModule(KotlinModule())` and avoid service discovery entirely. That reduces runtime surprises in shaded jars.

maria: good tips. I can try these: enable ServicesResourceTransformer in maven-shade, or remove `findAndRegisterModules()` and register explicitly. Also will try turning off followRedirects and see if it reproduces.

kevin: if you push a quick branch I can add a unit test that simulates an NDJSON stream + a relocated service file to reproduce. CI-bot: tagging the relevant PR template? :ci: 

ci-bot: linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/452 - added ServicesResourceTransformer + explicit module registration fallback.

maria: thanks all. tagging @jen for review after I open the PR. will update here after reproducing. :thumbsup:
